newsitem.title: USA: CME approves filing for boneless beef contracts.
newsitem.headline: CME approves filing for boneless beef contracts.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) plans to offer futures on boneless beef and beef trimmings contracts, the exchange said on Wednesday.

The exchange's board of directors approved regulatory filings for the contracts, the specifications of which would call for 20,000 pounds of fresh beef. The cash settlement feature would be based on a CME weighted average of prices from the USDA National Carlot Meat Report.
The contracts are revisions of dormant contracts which were traded on the CME in the 1970s and settled in frozen product, rather than fresh.
